newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- Hong Kong protest ships approached the disputed Diaoyu (Senkaku) Islands and were blocked by about 20 Japanese naval vessels.
-- Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng gave speeches saying the government would allocate more money to help develop poor regions.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS -- The Hong Kong inflation rate dropped to 4.9 percent, the lowest point in the past nine years. It was not expected to rise in the next three months.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Henderson Land's announcement to raise $3.5 billion via a placement and subscription raised doubts among securities analysts.

-- SING TAO DAILY -- Cheung Kong (Holdings) has decided to start its real estate agency business in October. Fifty branches would be set up within a year, and the number was expected to increase to 150 within three years.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- To help the development plan of its parent company in Beijing, Cosco Pacific planned to raise $1.55 billion by placing 250 million shares with institutions.
-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The former boss of Carrian, George Tan, could be forced to pay the $210 million it cost to bring him to justice.
-- Xiamen has called on Beijing for more power in drafting local laws relating to Taiwan.
-- English-language HONGKONG STANDARD -- Lawyers are pushing for the drafting of a code of conduct for judges to ensure the independence of the judiciary after the handover.
